joinSource.role: supplies the NDB numbers that ingredient ids are derived from

secondarySource.name: USDA FoodData Central - Foundation Foods
secondarySource.role: used only to identify ingredient codes that are valid NDB numbers outside SR Legacy; no id is emitted for them

provenance.citation: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service. FoodData Central, 2019. fdc.nal.usda.gov.
provenance.publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service

weightSemantics.whatGramsMeans: The gram weight of that ingredient in the recipe as USDA publishes it, before cooking. Recipes are stated at their own batch scale, not per 100 g of finished food.
weightSemantics.whyNotNormalised: Scaling the ingredient weights so they sum to 100 g, or to the dish's own finished weight, would discard the moisture change and misstate every ingredient. It would also be invisible: the numbers would still look like grams. The raw weights and the moisture factor are kept separate so any consumer that needs a finished-basis figure computes it explicitly.
weightSemantics.notCarried: input_food.portion_description is deliberately not carried. It names the portion-table row used for the unit conversion, not the recipe's own measure: a row reading amount=2.0 unit=C for celery carries portion_description '1 tablespoon' and gram_weight 240.0. gram_weight is the authoritative figure.
weightSemantics.portionsAre: Portions describe the FINISHED food, not the ingredient sum. Descriptions are verbatim from FNDDS and include its 'Quantity not specified' default.

idSemantics.fnddsFoodCodesAreNotCanonical: FNDDS food codes are not stable across releases -- over 1,800 were discontinued between two consecutive releases -- so they appear only under sourceRefsNotCanonical, together with the equally release-scoped FDC id.
idSemantics.catalogItemIdSchemeOwner: scripts/generate-catalog-from-srlegacy.py. This file follows it; it does not define it. ndbNumber is also carried verbatim so a consumer on a different scheme can rebuild the id without re-deriving the join.

ingredientReferenceKinds.sr_legacy_ndb: carries canonicalItemId in the catalog's scheme. NDB numbers survive record updates and are the documented join key to an SR-Legacy-backed catalog; SR Legacy's CSV stores them with leading zeros stripped, so they are zero-padded to the catalog's width to build the id and also carried verbatim as ndbNumber.
ingredientReferenceKinds.fndds_subrecipe: the ingredient is itself an FNDDS recipe in this file; dishId names it. Every such reference resolves within this file.
ingredientReferenceKinds.ndb_not_in_sr_legacy: a valid USDA NDB number that SR Legacy does not carry (it is a Foundation Foods record). No canonicalItemId is emitted, because an id pointing into a catalog built from SR Legacy would be a fabricated join.
ingredientReferenceKinds.fndds_pseudo_ingredient: an FNDDS bookkeeping entry rather than a food -- fortification lines such as 'Calcium as ingredient', and composite placeholders such as 'Beef as ingredient in recipes'. No food exists to point at.
ingredientReferenceKinds.unresolved: the source code matched no known namespace.

idSemantics.additionalDescriptionsAreNotSynonyms: additionalDescriptions is FNDDS's own field, verbatim. Some entries are genuine alternate names ('goulash' for 'Stew, beef') and some are disambiguation notes ('any 2 or more meats'). No attempt was made to tell them apart; feeding the field wholesale into a synonym table would put phrases like 'other or multiple meats' into search.

verification.method: For every recipe whose ingredients all resolve to SR Legacy, protein per 100 g of finished food was predicted from the ingredient gram weights under three competing finished-weight divisors and compared with the value FNDDS publishes for that food. Protein was chosen because FNDDS applies no cooking retention factor to it.
